answer: Interleaved arrival spacing. Each identity must present its first N actions at intervals drawn from a shared random schedule; agents whose timestamps cluster tighter than the schedule allows are throttled to a slow lane. Duplicates therefore cannot be spun up in parallel without paying wall-clock delay per clone. The copper cost is idle capacity held open during forced waits. An operator can still queue clones, but each one drags a fable of patience it cannot fake. Honest bursty workloads route through a jetty of deferred slots, trading latency for admission.
